newsitem.title: USA: GTE sees higher earnings in 1997-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GTE sees higher earnings in 1997-WSJ.

text.p: GTE Corp expects to report strong earnings and revenue growth next year as a result of good gains in its local telephone and wireless businesses as well as in new markets, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

At a closed-door meeting with analysts, the company said GTE's per-share earnings would grow by "not less than 10 percent for the foreseeable future." GTE disclosed its forecast in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday.

The company also projected that its revenue would grow by six to eight percent in 1997, it said. GTE reported an 8.8 percent increase in net income for the third quarter this year on a seven-percent increase in revenue, it added.

The newspaper said the company expected its domestic telephone revenue to increase by five percent to six percent in 1997. Half of the increase would come from GTE's main local telephone and wireless businesses, while the other half would come from "new initiatives" like long-distance services, video and the Internet.
